findings.title: newCheckout flag path is dead; only legacy/deprecated path ever runs

evidence.quote:
// newCheckout has been off since launch; the new flow was never finished
  newCheckout: false,

findings.note: Old path (100% of call sites: the single checkout() caller) runs through the deprecated legacyFormat helper; the new path guarded by newCheckout is unreachable and, per the comment, was abandoned rather than scheduled. No ticket or date is present for finishing or removing it.

findings.title: Deprecated legacyFormat still the only caller path, not formatMoney
findings.note: The only call site of legacyFormat (checkout.ts:11) still uses the deprecated wrapper instead of formatMoney directly; formatMoney has no callers outside the wrapper, so 100% of live call sites sit on the old side.

findings.title: tslint.json left in place after move to ESLint, with tslint not installed
findings.note: eslint is a devDependency and .eslintrc.json exists as the active successor config, but tslint.json (the superseded tool's config) is still checked in; tslint itself is absent from package.json and both lockfiles, and no lint script or CI step runs either config.

open_questions.question: Is there a tracked ticket/date to either finish or remove the newCheckout flow, or is it considered permanently abandoned?
Is tslint.json intentionally retained for a downstream consumer/tool, or is it simply forgotten cleanup from the ESLint migration?

looks_bad_but_fine.why: client.ts and client-admin.ts target distinct hosts (api.example.com vs admin.example.com) and are a duplication/coupling concern (drifted timeout/logging handling), not an old-vs-new migration pair; no naming or deprecation signal marks either as superseded.

not_assessed: Whether eslint 9.0.0 or the tslint config represent an EOL/deprecated dependency version in the security or support sense
Whether removing tslint.json or the newCheckout branch would affect any external tooling not visible in this repository
